#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SharkSight on one Google Compute Engine VM (D-062): Postgres + app + an HTTPS/password proxy via Docker Compose
# (deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/Caddyfile). Made for the Google Cloud free tier: one e2-micro (x86, 1 GB + 2 GB swap)
# with a 30 GB standard disk in us-central1 (free-tier regions: us-west1, us-central1, us-east1).
#
#   deploy/gcp/deploy.sh <command> [options]
#
#   check        prerequisites: gcloud logged in with a project, Compute Engine API on, Docker
#   create       SSH key, its own VPC network + firewall (SSH from your IP only, 80/443 open), the VM (Ubuntu 24.04,
#                Docker and 2 GB swap installed on first boot)
#   build        the app image for linux/amd64 (the Python part is emulated on an ARM Mac: a few minutes)
#   push         image (docker save | ssh docker load — no registry) + compose, Caddyfile, .env, data/settings.json,
#                data/models to the VM
#   up           start db + app (+ the HTTPS proxy unless --private); the app runs the schema migrations on start
#   data         copy the local database into the VM's (pg_dump → pg_restore, data only; refuses a non-empty
#                target, `data --replace` wipes it first)
#   deploy       build + push + up
#   url          address and login (kept in deploy/gcp/.env.vm)
#   status | logs | ssh
#   tunnel       SSH tunnel: app on http://127.0.0.1:8601, the VM's Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5434
#   budget       a $5 monthly budget alert (e-mails the billing account's admins)
#   allow-my-ip  re-open SSH for your current IP (after it changed)
#   stop | start     stop / start the VM (disk and data stay; the public IP changes → run `push` again for HTTPS)
#   destroy      delete the VM (its disk and all data on it), the firewall rules, the network and the SSH key
#
# Settings (environment): GCP_PROJECT (gcloud's current project), GCP_ZONE (us-central1-a), MACHINE_TYPE (e2-micro;
# e2-small = 2 GB if 1 GB is too tight, not free), NAME (sharksight).
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
HERE="$ROOT/deploy/gcp"
STACK="$ROOT/deploy"
PROJECT="${GCP_PROJECT:-$(gcloud config get-value project 2>/dev/null || true)}"
ZONE="${GCP_ZONE:-us-central1-a}"
TYPE="${MACHINE_TYPE:-e2-micro}"
NAME="${NAME:-sharksight}"
IMAGE="sharksight:prod-amd64"
KEY="$HERE/$NAME.key"                         # git-ignored (*.key), 0600
ENV_VM="$HERE/.env.vm"                        # secrets for the VM; git-ignored (.env.*), 0600
SSH_USER="sharksight"
REMOTE_DIR="sharksight"
PRIVATE=0
REPLACE=0

say()  { printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
need() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "$1 not found — $2"; }
gc()   { gcloud --project "$PROJECT" --quiet "$@"; }

vm_exists() { [[ -n "$(gc compute instances list --filter="name=$NAME" --format='value(name)' 2>/dev/null)" ]]; }

public_ip() {
  vm_exists || die "no VM named $NAME in $PROJECT — run: deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create"
  gc compute instances describe "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE" --format='get(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)'
}

my_ip() { curl -fsS https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '[:space:]'; }

ssh_opts() { echo "-i $KEY -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o UserKnownHostsFile=$HERE/.known_hosts -o ServerAliveInterval=30"; }

# Run a shell command in the deployment directory on the VM.
remote() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  ssh $(ssh_opts) "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)" \
    "mkdir -p ~/$REMOTE_DIR && cd ~/$REMOTE_DIR && COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=sharksight DOCKER='sudo docker' bash -c $(printf '%q' "$1")"
}

# Copy local files into the deployment directory (keeps the last path component).
remote_copy() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  scp $(ssh_opts) -r -C "$@" "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip):$REMOTE_DIR/"
}

# Stream stdin into a command on the VM.
remote_pipe() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  ssh $(ssh_opts) "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)" "$1"
}

env_get() { grep -E "^$1=" "$2" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ commands
cmd_check() {
  need docker "install Docker Desktop or OrbStack"
  need gcloud "brew install --cask google-cloud-sdk, then: gcloud auth login && gcloud config set project <id>"
  [[ -f "$ROOT/.env" ]] || die "no .env at the repo root (see .env.example)"
  [[ -n "$PROJECT" ]] || die "no project: gcloud config set project <id> (or GCP_PROJECT=<id>)"
  local who; who="$(gcloud config get-value account 2>/dev/null)"; [[ -n "$who" ]] || die "not logged in: gcloud auth login"
  gc services list --enabled --filter=name:compute.googleapis.com --format='value(name)' | grep -q compute \
    || { say "enabling the Compute Engine API (needs billing on the project)…"; gc services enable compute.googleapis.com; }
  say "account $who, project $PROJECT, zone $ZONE, machine type $TYPE"
  say "ok"
}

cmd_create() {
  vm_exists && die "a VM named $NAME already exists in $PROJECT"
  if [[ ! -f "$KEY" ]]; then
    say "SSH key $KEY…"
    ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C "$SSH_USER" -f "$KEY"
  fi
  # Its own network: the default network has an "SSH from anywhere" rule, this one only opens what we add.
  if ! gc compute networks describe "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    say "network $NAME + firewall (SSH from your IP, 80/443 open)…"
    gc compute networks create "$NAME" --subnet-mode=auto >/dev/null
    gc compute firewall-rules create "$NAME-web" --network "$NAME" --allow tcp:80,tcp:443 \
      --source-ranges 0.0.0.0/0 --target-tags "$NAME" >/dev/null
  fi
  cmd_allow_my_ip
  local startup keys
  startup="$(mktemp)"; keys="$(mktemp)"
  cat > "$startup" <<'EOS'
#!/bin/bash
set -e
if ! command -v docker >/dev/null; then curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh; fi
if [ ! -f /swapfile ]; then
  fallocate -l 2G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap /swapfile && swapon /swapfile
  echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' >> /etc/fstab
fi
EOS
  echo "$SSH_USER:$(cat "$KEY.pub")" > "$keys"
  say "VM $TYPE in $ZONE (Ubuntu 24.04, 30 GB standard disk)…"
  gc compute instances create "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE" --machine-type "$TYPE" \
    --network "$NAME" --tags "$NAME" --labels project=sharksight \
    --image-family ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64 --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 30GB --boot-disk-type pd-standard \
    --metadata enable-oslogin=FALSE --metadata-from-file "startup-script=$startup,ssh-keys=$keys" >/dev/null
  rm -f "$startup" "$keys"
  say "running at $(public_ip). Docker installs on first boot (~2 min); then: deploy/gcp/deploy.sh deploy"
}

cmd_allow_my_ip() {
  local ip; ip="$(my_ip)"
  if gc compute firewall-rules describe "$NAME-ssh" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gc compute firewall-rules update "$NAME-ssh" --source-ranges "$ip/32" >/dev/null
  else
    gc compute firewall-rules create "$NAME-ssh" --network "$NAME" --allow tcp:22 \
      --source-ranges "$ip/32" --target-tags "$NAME" >/dev/null
  fi
  say "SSH open for $ip"
}

cmd_build() {
  say "building $IMAGE (linux/amd64)…"
  docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --target prod -t "$IMAGE" --load "$ROOT"
}

write_env() {
  # Secrets for the VM, from the local .env; the web login is generated once and kept in .env.vm.
  local ip site user pw hash
  ip="$(public_ip)"
  site="${ip//./-}.sslip.io"   # HTTPS via sslip.io
  user="$(env_get BASIC_AUTH_USER "$ENV_VM")"; user="${user:-pm}"
  pw="$(env_get WEB_PASSWORD "$ENV_VM")"
  [[ -n "$pw" ]] || pw="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"   # no pipe: under pipefail a SIGPIPE'd generator would end the script
  hash="$(docker run --rm caddy:2.10-alpine caddy hash-password --plaintext "$pw")"
  ( umask 077
    { echo "# generated by deploy/gcp/deploy.sh — secrets for the VM, never commit"
      for k in OPENAI_API_KEY OPENAI_MODEL_FAST OPENAI_MODEL_SMART OPENAI_MODEL_EMBED POSTGRES_PASSWORD APP_DB_PASSWORD; do
        echo "$k=$(env_get "$k" "$ROOT/.env")"
      done
      echo "APP_IMAGE=$IMAGE"
      echo "SITE_ADDRESS=$site"
      echo "BASIC_AUTH_USER=$user"
      echo "BASIC_AUTH_HASH='$hash'"   # single quotes: compose must not expand the $ in the bcrypt hash
      echo "WEB_PASSWORD=$pw"          # for you; the proxy only knows the hash
    } > "$ENV_VM" )
}

cmd_push() {
  [[ -n "$(docker images -q "$IMAGE")" ]] || die "no $IMAGE image — run: deploy/gcp/deploy.sh build"
  remote 'command -v docker >/dev/null' || die "Docker is not installed on the VM yet — wait a minute after create"
  write_env
  say "sending the image…"
  docker save "$IMAGE" | gzip -1 | remote_pipe "gunzip | sudo docker load"
  local staged; staged="$(mktemp -d)"
  cp "$STACK/compose.yaml" "$STACK/Caddyfile" "$staged/"
  cp "$ENV_VM" "$staged/.env"
  mkdir -p "$staged/data" "$staged/restore"
  [[ -f "$ROOT/data/settings.json" ]] && cp "$ROOT/data/settings.json" "$staged/data/"
  [[ -d "$ROOT/data/models" ]] && cp -R "$ROOT/data/models" "$staged/data/"
  say "copying compose, Caddyfile, .env, settings and 3D models…"
  remote_copy "$staged/compose.yaml" "$staged/Caddyfile" "$staged/.env" "$staged/data" "$staged/restore"
  rm -rf "$staged"
  remote 'chmod 600 .env'
}

cmd_up() {
  local profile=""; [[ $PRIVATE == 1 ]] || profile="--profile public"
  remote "\$DOCKER compose $profile up -d && \$DOCKER compose ps --format '{{.Name}} {{.Status}}'"
  if [[ $PRIVATE == 1 ]]; then say "private: reach it with deploy/gcp/deploy.sh tunnel"; else cmd_url; fi
}

cmd_data() {
  say "dumping the local database…"
  make -C "$ROOT" backup >/dev/null
  local dump; dump="$(ls -t "$ROOT"/data/backups/sharksight-*.dump | head -1)"
  remote "\$DOCKER compose up -d --wait db app >/dev/null"   # the app creates the schema (migrations) on start
  local rows
  rows="$(remote "\$DOCKER compose exec -T db psql -U sharksight -d sharksight -tAc 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_item'" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  if [[ "$rows" != "0" ]]; then
    [[ $REPLACE == 1 ]] || die "the VM's database already holds $rows source items — use: deploy/gcp/deploy.sh data --replace"
    say "wiping the VM's database…"
    remote "\$DOCKER compose down && \$DOCKER volume rm sharksight_pgdata && \$DOCKER compose up -d --wait db app >/dev/null"
  fi
  say "copying $(basename "$dump") ($(du -h "$dump" | cut -f1))…"
  remote_copy "$dump"
  remote "mv $(basename "$dump") restore/db.dump && \$DOCKER compose stop app >/dev/null && \
    \$DOCKER compose exec -T db sh -c 'pg_restore -l /restore/db.dump | grep -v alembic_version > /tmp/list && \
      pg_restore -U sharksight -d sharksight --data-only --disable-triggers --single-transaction -L /tmp/list /restore/db.dump' && \
    rm -f restore/db.dump && \$DOCKER compose start app >/dev/null && \
    \$DOCKER compose exec -T db psql -U sharksight -d sharksight -tAc \"SELECT 'source items: ' || COUNT(*) FROM source_item\""
  say "data copied"
}

cmd_url() {
  local site user pw
  site="$(env_get SITE_ADDRESS "$ENV_VM")"; user="$(env_get BASIC_AUTH_USER "$ENV_VM")"; pw="$(env_get WEB_PASSWORD "$ENV_VM")"
  say "https://$site   login: $user / $pw   (the HTTPS certificate takes a minute on first start)"
}

cmd_tunnel() {
  say "app → http://127.0.0.1:8601   Postgres → 127.0.0.1:5434 (Ctrl-C to close)"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  ssh $(ssh_opts) -N -L 8601:127.0.0.1:8600 -L 5434:127.0.0.1:5432 "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)"
}

cmd_budget() {
  local account
  account="$(gcloud billing projects describe "$PROJECT" --format='value(billingAccountName)' | sed 's#billingAccounts/##')"
  [[ -n "$account" ]] || die "project $PROJECT has no billing account linked"
  gc services enable billingbudgets.googleapis.com
  gcloud billing budgets create --billing-account "$account" --display-name sharksight-5usd \
    --budget-amount 5USD --filter-projects "projects/$PROJECT" \
    --threshold-rule percent=0.5 --threshold-rule percent=0.8 --threshold-rule percent=1.0 >/dev/null
  say "budget sharksight-5usd: e-mails to the billing admins at 50 / 80 / 100 % of \$5 a month"
}

cmd_destroy() {
  read -r -p "Delete $NAME in $PROJECT (its disk and ALL data on it), its firewall rules, network and SSH key? [y/N] " ok
  [[ "$ok" == y ]] || exit 1
  vm_exists && gc compute instances delete "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE"
  for r in "$NAME-web" "$NAME-ssh"; do gc compute firewall-rules delete "$r" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  gc compute networks delete "$NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$KEY" "$KEY.pub" "$HERE/.known_hosts"
  say "destroyed"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ main
cmd="${1:-help}"; shift || true
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in --private) PRIVATE=1 ;; --replace) REPLACE=1 ;; *) die "unknown option $a" ;; esac
done
case "$cmd" in
  check|create|build|push|up|data|url|tunnel|budget|destroy) "cmd_$cmd" ;;
  allow-my-ip) cmd_allow_my_ip ;;
  deploy) cmd_build; cmd_push; cmd_up ;;
  status) remote '$DOCKER compose ps' ;;
  logs)   remote '$DOCKER compose logs --tail 200' ;;
  ssh)    # shellcheck disable=SC2046
          ssh $(ssh_opts) "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)" ;;
  stop)   gc compute instances stop "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE" && say "stopped (disk and data stay)" ;;
  start)  gc compute instances start "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE" \
            && say "running at $(public_ip) — the IP changed: run push (new HTTPS address), then up" ;;
  *) sed -n '2,27p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' ;;
esac

my_ip() { curl -fsS https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '[:space:]'; }

    || { say "enabling the Compute Engine API (needs billing on the project)…"; gc services enable compute.googleapis.com; }

  say "VM $TYPE in $ZONE (Ubuntu 24.04, 30 GB standard disk)…"
  gc compute instances create "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE" --machine-type "$TYPE" \
    --network "$NAME" --tags "$NAME" --labels project=sharksight \
    --image-family ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64 --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 30GB --boot-disk-type pd-standard \
    --metadata enable-oslogin=FALSE --metadata-from-file "startup-script=$startup,ssh-keys=$keys" >/dev/null

cmd_url() {

  [[ -n "$account" ]] || die "project $PROJECT has no billing account linked"
  gc services enable billingbudgets.googleapis.com
  gcloud billing budgets create --billing-account "$account" --display-name sharksight-5usd \
    --budget-amount 5USD --filter-projects "projects/$PROJECT" \
    --threshold-rule percent=0.5 --threshold-rule percent=0.8 --threshold-rule percent=1.0 >/dev/null
  say "budget sharksight-5usd: e-mails to the billing admins at 50 / 80 / 100 % of \$5 a month"
}

cmd_destroy() {
  read -r -p "Delete $NAME in $PROJECT (its disk and ALL data on it), its firewall rules, network and SSH key? [y/N] " ok
  [[ "$ok" == y ]] || exit 1
  vm_exists && gc compute instances delete "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE"
  for r in "$NAME-web" "$NAME-ssh"; do gc compute firewall-rules delete "$r" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  gc compute networks delete "$NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$KEY" "$KEY.pub" "$HERE/.known_hosts"
  say "destroyed"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ main
cmd="${1:-help}"; shift || true
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in --private) PRIVATE=1 ;; --replace) REPLACE=1 ;; *) die "unknown option $a" ;; esac
done
case "$cmd" in
  check|create|build|push|up|data|url|tunnel|budget|destroy) "cmd_$cmd" ;;
  allow-my-ip) cmd_allow_my_ip ;;
  deploy) cmd_build; cmd_push; cmd_up ;;
  status) remote '$DOCKER compose ps' ;;
  logs)   remote '$DOCKER compose logs --tail 200' ;;
  ssh)    # shellcheck disable=SC2046
          ssh $(ssh_opts) "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)" ;;
  stop)   gc compute instances stop "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE" && say "stopped (disk and data stay)" ;;
  start)  gc compute instances start "$NAME" --zone "$ZONE" \
            && say "running at $(public_ip) — the IP changed: run push (new HTTPS address), then up" ;;
  *) sed -n '2,27p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' ;;
esac

# Deploying SharkSight to Google Cloud (D-062)

One Compute Engine VM runs the same containers as your laptop: **db** (PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector), **app** (API + the
built PM app) and a small **proxy** (Caddy: HTTPS + one password, because the app has no login of its own yet).

```
deploy/compose.yaml   the stack on the VM (provider-neutral)
deploy/Caddyfile      HTTPS for <ip>.sslip.io + basic auth in front of the app
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh  the CLI: create the VM, ship the image and files, start, copy data, tunnel, destroy
deploy/aws/deploy.sh  the same for one AWS EC2 instance (D-061, not used: Atahan dropped AWS)
```

## Cost

Made for the **Google Cloud free tier**: one e2-micro VM (2 shared vCPUs, 1 GB RAM) and 30 GB of standard disk are
free every month in `us-west1`, `us-central1` or `us-east1`, plus 1 GB of outbound traffic. A public IPv4 address may
be billed (a few dollars a month). New accounts also get a **$300 / 90-day trial credit**; as long as you don't
upgrade to a paid account, nothing is charged when it runs out. `deploy.sh budget` adds a $5 monthly alert.

1 GB is tight for Postgres + the app: the VM gets 2 GB of swap and Postgres is tuned small. If it is too slow,
`MACHINE_TYPE=e2-small` (2 GB, ≈ $12 / month, from the trial credit) — `destroy`, then `create` with it.

## One-time setup (you)

1. Create a Google Cloud account at https://console.cloud.google.com (card needed for verification; trial credit).
2. Create a project (e.g. `sharksight`) and make sure billing is linked to it.
3. On this Mac: `brew install --cask google-cloud-sdk`, then `gcloud auth login` and
   `gcloud config set project <project-id>`.
4. `deploy/gcp/deploy.sh check` (also switches on the Compute Engine API)

## Deploy

```bash
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create          # SSH key, network + firewall, e2-micro (Ubuntu 24.04); wait ~2 min for Docker
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh deploy          # build the x86 image, send it + compose + .env + settings + 3D models, start
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh data            # copy your local database into the VM (once; --replace to overwrite)
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh url             # https://<ip>.sslip.io — user pm, password in deploy/gcp/.env.vm
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh budget
```

After a code change: `deploy/gcp/deploy.sh deploy` again (data stays; the app migrates the schema on start).

## Day to day

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status`, `logs`, `ssh` | container state, last 200 log lines, a shell on the VM |
| `tunnel` | app on http://127.0.0.1:8601 and the VM's Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5434 — e.g. run a pipeline stage from this Mac against the cloud database with `DATABASE_URL=REDACTED` |
| `up --private` | db + app only, no public proxy; use `tunnel` to reach it |
| `allow-my-ip` | your IP changed and SSH is refused |
| `stop` / `start` | pause the VM (disk and data stay; the public IP changes → `push` then `up`) |
| `destroy` | delete the VM and its disk (all cloud data), firewall rules, network and SSH key |

Settings: `GCP_PROJECT` (default: gcloud's current project), `GCP_ZONE` (`us-central1-a`), `MACHINE_TYPE` (`e2-micro`).

## What is where

- Secrets: `deploy/gcp/.env.vm` (generated from your `.env`: OpenAI key, database passwords, the web login) and the SSH
  key `deploy/gcp/sharksight.key` — both git-ignored, 0600. On the VM they are `~sharksight/sharksight/.env`.
- Ports: the VM has its own network `sharksight` (not the default one, which allows SSH from anywhere): only 80/443
  (proxy) are open to the world, SSH only from your IP; the app (8600) and Postgres (5432) listen on the VM's localhost.
- The image is built for linux/amd64; on an ARM Mac the Python part is emulated (the frontend builds natively).

## Before anyone else uses it

The proxy password is shared, so the audit trail still records whatever name the browser sends (`X-Actor`). Real
logins for people, app settings in the database instead of `data/settings.json`, and the 3D models in object storage
are the next steps for a proper deployment (STATE → Next up).

content.text:
I added a Google Cloud deploy script, `deploy/gcp/deploy.sh`. It runs the same setup as the AWS one (database, app, and an HTTPS front door with a password) on Google's free e2-micro server. I haven't run it against Google Cloud yet because you don't have an account set up. What I did test: the x86 version of the app image builds on your Mac, its Python code loads, and the frontend is included. The upload and database-copy steps are copied from the AWS script, which was tested end to end on the Mac.

**What you need to do first:**
1. Create a Google Cloud account at console.cloud.google.com. New accounts get a $300 credit for 90 days, and nothing is charged afterwards unless you upgrade to a paid account. Then create a project and make sure billing is linked to it.
2. On the Mac:
   ```
   brew install --cask google-cloud-sdk
   gcloud auth login
   gcloud config set project <your-project-id>
   ```

**Then deploy:**
```
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh check     # also switches on the Compute Engine API
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create    # creates the server; wait ~2 min for Docker to install
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh deploy    # builds and uploads the app, then starts it
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh data      # copies your local database up
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh url       # https://<ip>.sslip.io, user pm; the password is in deploy/gcp/.env.vm
```

**Worth knowing:**
- **Memory is tight.** The free server has 1 GB of RAM. I added 2 GB of swap and Postgres is set up to use little memory. If it's too slow, run `destroy`, then `MACHINE_TYPE=e2-small deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create` (2 GB, about $12/month, paid from the trial credit).
- **The data will be in the US.** Google's free tier only covers US regions, so this uses `us-central1`. A Frankfurt server (`GCP_ZONE=europe-west3-a`) works but isn't free.
- **The public IP address may cost a few dollars a month.** The trial credit covers that.
- **SSH is open only from your IP.** The server gets its own network, because Google's default network allows SSH from anywhere.
- **The Dockerfile has one change:** the frontend now builds natively, so only the Python part is emulated for x86. This doesn't affect the ARM build.

I logged the decision as D-062, which replaces the AWS one (D-061), and updated `deploy/README.md`, STATE, Q-028, the tech-stack doc, README and AGENTS rule 1. The AWS script is still in `deploy/aws/`; say if you want it deleted. Nothing is committed.

**One problem in the earlier uncommitted changes:** they reused the number Q-028 for the cloud question. That deleted the open question "Generalize SharkSight beyond BMW into a domain-agnostic product", which had links to your market-scan artifacts. I haven't touched it. Should I restore that question under a new number (Q-029)?

## Open

### Q-027 — Continuous data intake instead of fixed checkpoints (future)
- Owner: Atahan · not blocking · raised 2026-10-11
- Atahan: the two fixed checkpoints (D-040) will eventually go; new data should be digested automatically — e.g. a background agent that searches the web from time to time, and the user uploading new data into the knowledge base.
- Open: how evidence is versioned without checkpoints (rolling snapshots? event time?), what a "run" is then, how the audit trail and the PM's decisions stay comparable over time, upload formats + validation + confidentiality (rule 1), and the cost cap for a background agent (D-054/D-055 limits apply).
- Until then the Audit page and every screen keep the per-checkpoint separation (D-055).

### Q-026 — Gaps in the checkpoint research (D-040)
- The agents' web-search quota ran out mid-run. Missing: China model-level sales (5 Series LWB / E-Class L / A6L; Gasgoo/CPCA rankings blocked), Japan & Korea market totals, UK/EU-wide model rankings (Dataforce/JATO), Genesis/Lincoln H1 2026, BMW 1/7 Series volumes in EU/CN, Chinese vs foreign brand share in China, China subsidy pauses, Germany EV-subsidy uptake, UK ZEV mandate, charging-cost vs fuel, in-car AI adoption data, OTA/subscriptions. Full list: `gaps` in `research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json`.
- **China round 2 done (2026-10-11):** +207 items (china_models, china_market, china_context): FY2025/H1 2026 retail for A6L / E-Class / 5 Series, luxury registrations 7 Series / S-Class / S800 / Maybach S, domestic-brand share 64→69 %, luxury retail −30 % in H1, CPCA forecast cut, trade-in fund, L2/NOA standard, McKinsey 2026. Many China model figures are Yiche sums (T3, unverified). Still open: i7 China, BBA combined share, rear-screen/massage penetration, Roland Berger/Bain, Gasgoo (blocked).

### Q-025 — 3D models for the Cars screen (D-039)
- Owner: Atahan · not blocking (placeholder car renders without them)
- Context: the Cars screen renders public, fan-made CC BY Sketchfab models (attribution on screen): 1 Series "Bmw-1-series 2025" (teenlin3, AI-generated mesh, 500k tris), 5 Series "i5" (akyolefe319), 7 Series "2023 BMW I7 G70" (NazhDesign). Downloads need a Sketchfab login (the agent may not log in), so the files must be placed in `data/models/{f70,g60,g70}.glb` (or `<name>/scene.gltf`). Each model's axis orientation in `car_zones.MODELS_GLTF` is provisional until checked visually. For real use BMW would supply its own visualisation assets.
- Update 2026-10-11: Atahan downloaded the three GLBs; copied (not moved — raw folder is read-only) to `data/models/{f70,g60,g70}.glb`; orientations set in `car_zones.MODELS_GLTF` (files carry a Z-up→Y-up root matrix → F70/G70 front +z, G60 front −z) and checked by rendering all three plus the rear-cabin x-ray. Remaining: whether to keep these fan-made models for the pitch (the 1 Series mesh is AI-generated) and the originals in `challange information document/` can be deleted by Atahan.

### Q-005 — How are the "Source A–D" feedback channels interpreted?

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

web

## Stack

React + TypeScript (Vite) frontend with three.js via react-three-fiber for real-time 3D; a small FastAPI JSON layer (`backend/src/api/`) over the existing Python pipeline (`backend/src/bmw_req`, PostgreSQL + pgvector, D-059). Chosen by Atahan on 2026-10-11 to replace the Streamlit UI (D-039). Runs locally only (confidential BMW data, AGENTS rule 1).

## Users

- **Primary: a BMW product manager (PM)** responsible for what the successor of a car line (1, 5, 7 Series) offers its customers in each market. Over a ~2-year process they review AI-drafted customer requirements, decide (approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge, always with a reason), set priorities per car × market, and hand the result to engineering — while new evidence keeps arriving.
- **Demo audience: BMW judges and mentors** of the "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon, watching the PM (Atahan) work the tool live on a laptop or projector. The UI is tuned demo-first: the story must land in a few clicks, without breaking the real tool underneath.

## Product Purpose

Turn ~10k customer comments, a customer study, sales data, option lists and cited web research into prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements for successor BMW cars, per car and market. The AI reads, groups, drafts, checks fit and scores; the PM decides; everything is traceable to the customer's words and audited. Success: a PM trusts and acts on the ranking because every number explains itself, and the judges see a living decision process, not a one-shot list.

## Positioning

Not a feedback dashboard and not a chatbot: a decision instrument. Every requirement is a product decision BMW could take or trade off, scored per market with a visible factor breakdown, traced down to individual comments, gated by brand fit, and re-proposed — never silently changed — as new evidence arrives in waves.

## Operating Context

- Simulated ~2-year process: three evidence waves (feedback has no dates), each re-scoring and producing AI change proposals the PM accepts or rejects.
- Portfolio: F70 (1 Series), G60 (5 Series), G68 (5 Series LWB, China), G70 (7 Series); markets USA, Europe, China, Rest of world.
- Hand-offs: defect-type pain goes to a Quality hand-over list, not into requirements; the approved list is exported.
- Today's car matters as a reference: the current car and its equipment (German price list; public BMW configurator) are the baseline the successor improves on.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- AI only proposes; approved/rejected/deferred need a named human and a rationale. Brand-fit FAIL blocks approval unless the PM overrides with a reason. Audit is append-only.
- Scope: customer-facing requirements only — no regulatory, engineering specs or pricing.
- Evidence and assumption are always shown apart; conflicting evidence is surfaced, not hidden; markets without own comments are labelled.
- OpenAI is the only LLM provider; $100 total budget; running a wave costs money and takes minutes.
- Terminology to keep (English): Must / Should / Could; "5 Series · USA"; Strong / Good / Limited evidence / Assumption only; Expected / Differentiator / Delighter; To review / Challenged / Approved / Deferred / Rejected; "AI suggests" for unconfirmed priorities.
- A parallel workstream (D-040+) adds requirement origins (competitors, trends, regulation, personas), a regulatory radar, customer & model groups, an offering matrix per market and market intelligence; the IA must have a home for these.

## Brand Commitments

- English UI, current domain terms.
- Dark theme only.
- A BMW-like blue accent is wanted.
- No BMW logo or trademark branding in the UI; neutral product name.

## Evidence on Hand

- Live database (PostgreSQL in Docker): 10,128 verbatims, 1,369 cited research / web / reference items, study metrics, sales, option lists; 15,440 classified signals; 76 (JAN 26) / 80 (JUL 26) requirements and 252 / 259 prioritized line × market targets; ~2.9k audit events. Verbatims are BMW-confidential: localhost only.
- 3D models of today's cars: public CC BY Sketchfab models (attribution required), downloaded by Atahan into `data/models/` (Q-025). Fan-made approximations, not BMW CAD.
- No testimonials, user research or production usage exist — never fabricate them.

## Product Principles

1. The PM decides, the AI explains — every AI output is a proposal with its cause visible.
2. One number, fully opened — any score can be unfolded to its factors and down to the customer's words.
3. Markets are different customers — never average them away; show where they disagree.
4. The car is the canvas — requirements are about a physical product; show them on it.
5. A process, not a report — what changed since last time comes first.

| Deadline / judging | none — hackathon over |

## Done

Post-hackathon (2026-10-11 / 12):
- Repo cleanup + monorepo layout `backend/` / `frontend/` (D-052); run profiles + containers (D-053).
- Adjustable budget + API key in the app (D-054); AI agents page as the source of truth for models, efforts, caps (D-055); Audit page per checkpoint (D-055); full-screen 2D pages (D-056).
- Wave pipeline retired and its tables dropped (D-057, D-058); LangGraph removed.
- PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector (D-059): migrations, compatibility layer, data copied and verified (99 API answers identical), timestamptz, exact vector search in SQL, restricted app role, SQLite removed.
- No sample data anywhere in the app (D-060).

Hackathon:
- Challenge analyzed; all BMW data profiled and re-verified (`documents/data-inventory.md`).
- Foundation, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` created.
- BMW mentor input recorded (D-011 markets differ, D-012 future needs, D-013 continuous re-prioritization). BMW support recommended the annual report → `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md`.
- Model tiering (D-010); budget re-baselined (D-014).
- Q-001/002/003 answered by Atahan → D-005 (portfolio-level, 5 Series deepest), D-006 (OpenAI), D-007 (web knowledge base), D-008 (brand fit gate), D-009 (plant/platform feasibility).
- Conceptual architecture, requirement model and knowledge-base design drafted. Tech stack decided 2026-10-10 (D-015–D-020).
- Web research seeds written and fact-checked:
  - `portfolio-reference.md`: platforms, 14 vehicle plants + 3 CKD sites, BMW sales 2024–H1 2026, primary-sourced from the annual report where possible.
  - `competitor-landscape.md`: competitors, trends, expectations, brand-fit guardrails.
- Foundation review (2026-10-10) fixed, except the confidentiality items, which Atahan dropped.

## In progress

Nothing running.

## How to run

- **Database first:** `make db`, then `make migrate` (PostgreSQL in Docker, 127.0.0.1:5433, D-059). Back up with `make backup` (`pg_dump` → `data/backups/`); `make testdata` refreshes the real-data copy the API tests clone.
- **PM app:** production `make serve` or `make up` (container) → http://127.0.0.1:8600; development `make api` + `make dev` or `make up-dev` → http://127.0.0.1:5173. Only one at a time (same port, same database). All `uv run …` commands run from `backend/`.
- **Pipeline stages:** `uv run python -m bmw_req.structure.run_all`, `… -m bmw_req.definition.run --checkpoint cp1`, `… -m bmw_req.prioritize.run --checkpoint cp1` (then `cp2`); spend is guarded by the limits and agent settings on the AI agents page.
- **Cloud (Google Cloud):** `deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create` → `deploy` → `data` (D-062, guide `deploy/README.md`); needs gcloud logged in with a project (`gcloud auth login`, `gcloud config set project <id>`). The AWS script (D-061) is kept but unused.
- **3D models:** `data/models/{f70,g60,g70}.glb` (git-ignored, Q-025); without them a placeholder car renders.
- `data/backups/` holds the `pg_dump` backups (no SQLite files remain, 2026-10-12).

## Next up (suggested order)

1. **Automatic checks:** CI (GitHub workflow: pytest on a Postgres service + frontend typecheck) and a Python linter; fix the 3 lint findings that predate the cleanup (`run_all.py`, `prioritize/score.py`).
2. **AI output quality:** the weakest judged dimensions were "measurable" and "evidence-grounded"; terse audit text for the prioritize stage ("scored", "auto rescore").
3. **Continuous intake design** (Q-027): background web agent, uploads to the knowledge base, versioning without fixed checkpoints, job queue in Postgres; add the HNSW index when nodes pass ~50k.
4. **Login / roles for people** before anyone else uses the app.
5. **Open with BMW / Atahan:** Q-005, Q-006, Q-015, Q-016; sign-off of the brand guardrails (D-031), which gate approval.

## Budget (OpenAI — limits adjustable in the app, D-054; was $100 total, D-014)

| Item | Value |

## Risks / watch-outs

- Local anaconda Python 3.9 has a broken pandas/numpy → use `uv venv --python 3.12`.
- Option lists are German-market only — the US/CN equipment baseline is an assumption.
- Plant capacity/flexibility is rarely public → feasibility checks need explicit assumptions (Q-011).
- BMW says engineering is out of scope → keep feasibility framed as a filter (Q-010).
- BMW data must never be committed or sent anywhere except OpenAI (AGENTS rule 1).
- Public sales are only in model-series pairs, with no regional per-model figures. Model-level market volume relies on BMW's `sales_volumes.xlsx`, which looks stylized and conflicts with public China data (Q-015).
- Markets without own comments (CN) or very few (G70 EU) score on borrowed customer voice at half weight (D-038, prio-v1).
- Feedback data has no dates → the process runs on two real-date checkpoints (D-040); continuous intake is Q-027.
- China-built i5 (G68 BEV) reportedly ended Jul 2026 (insider rumour, unconfirmed by BMW as of 2026-10-10) — affects 5 Series China powertrain assumptions.
- X5/7 Series successors: BMW calls them NK models, trade press says the platform is CLAR-derived (`bmw-annual-report-2025.md` §4). This matters for the G70 successor.

## How to run

- **Database first:** `make db`, then `make migrate` (PostgreSQL in Docker, 127.0.0.1:5433, D-059). Back up with `make backup` (`pg_dump` → `data/backups/`); `make testdata` refreshes the real-data copy the API tests clone.
- **PM app:** production `make serve` or `make up` (container) → http://127.0.0.1:8600; development `make api` + `make dev` or `make up-dev` → http://127.0.0.1:5173. Only one at a time (same port, same database). All `uv run …` commands run from `backend/`.
- **Pipeline stages:** `uv run python -m bmw_req.structure.run_all`, `… -m bmw_req.definition.run --checkpoint cp1`, `… -m bmw_req.prioritize.run --checkpoint cp1` (then `cp2`); spend is guarded by the limits and agent settings on the AI agents page.
- **Cloud (Google Cloud):** `deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create` → `deploy` → `data` (D-062, guide `deploy/README.md`); needs gcloud logged in with a project (`gcloud auth login`, `gcloud config set project <id>`). The AWS script (D-061) is kept but unused.
- **3D models:** `data/models/{f70,g60,g70}.glb` (git-ignored, Q-025); without them a placeholder car renders.
- `data/backups/` holds the `pg_dump` backups (no SQLite files remain, 2026-10-12).

## Why now (future needs → what covers them)

| Need | SQLite today | PostgreSQL |
|---|---|---|
| Background agents writing while the PM works (Q-027) | one writer at a time | MVCC, concurrent writers |
| Scheduled / queued agent jobs | in-process threads | a job table with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` |
| Semantic search over the knowledge base (RAG) | numpy brute force over BLOBs | `pgvector` + HNSW index, hybrid with full-text search |
| Uploads to the knowledge base | files would bloat the DB file | files on disk / object storage; provenance, chunks, embeddings in Postgres |
| Evidence graph | edge tables | edge tables + `WITH RECURSIVE` (graph queries in SQL) |
| Tamper-proof audit trail | triggers | triggers + the app role has no UPDATE / DELETE on audit tables |
| Several users, login, remote access | a local file | roles, network access, managed hosting possible (only with BMW's OK, rule 1) |
| Schema evolution | hand-rolled `MIGRATIONS` list + `ensure()` per module | versioned Alembic migrations, one place |

## Starting point (measured 2026-10-12)

---

## Out of scope here

Continuous intake, the job queue and uploads (Q-027) — this migration only makes them possible. Login / roles for
people (needed before any shared deployment).

## P0 as built (2026-10-12)
---
- **Vector search:** `contextualize.candidates` asks Postgres for the K nearest evidence nodes per type (`ORDER BY
  embedding <=> theme, node_id DESC`), exact. `scripts/check_retrieval.py` compared it with the numpy search it
  replaced: 178 of 178 themes (cp1 71, cp2 107) identical. **No HNSW index yet, on purpose:** 2,192 nodes take
  milliseconds exactly, and an approximate index could return other neighbours. Add `CREATE INDEX … USING hnsw
  (embedding vector_cosine_ops)` with `hnsw.iterative_scan` when the knowledge base grows past ~50k nodes (Q-027), and
  re-run the check. Clustering and the 3D layout need full matrices and stay in numpy.
- **Bug found:** pgvector returns `Vector` objects, not numpy arrays — every pipeline step reading embeddings would

I moved all the vision and future-work content into one file, `foundation/documents/future-work.md`, and removed it everywhere else. That file is marked as parked for another repo, so agents won't act on it here.

**What went into the new file:**
- **The idea of a general-purpose SharkSight beyond BMW** (the old Q-028), including both market-scan links. Earlier uncommitted edits had already deleted this question from the open list, so I recovered it from git.
- **Continuous data intake** (Q-027), plus its item in STATE's "Next up" list.
- **The "parallel workstream" note from `PRODUCT.md`** (regulatory radar, offering matrix and so on).

**What I removed or repointed:**
- Q-027 is gone from the open questions, and the two log entries about the general-purpose version are gone from STATE.
- `postgres-migration.md` and a STATE risk line now point to the new file instead of to Q-027.
- I added the new file to the reading table in AGENTS.md and to the folder map in `foundation/README.md`.
- The cloud question had reused the number Q-028, so I renumbered it to Q-029.

lines: -#!/usr/bin/env bash
-# SharkSight on one AWS EC2 instance (D-061): Postgres + app + an HTTPS/password proxy via Docker Compose
-# (deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/Caddyfile). Made for the AWS Free plan: one t4g.small (ARM, 2 GB) in eu-central-1.
-#   deploy/aws/deploy.sh <command> [options]
-#   check        prerequisites: AWS CLI logged in, Docker
-#   create       key pair, security group (SSH from your IP only, 80/443 open), the instance (Ubuntu 24.04 ARM,
-#                20 GB gp3, Docker, 2 GB swap, CPU credits "standard" so it can't burst into extra charges)
-#   build        the app image for linux/arm64 (native on this Mac)
-#   push         image (docker save | ssh docker load — no registry) + compose, Caddyfile, .env, data/settings.json,
-#                data/models to the instance
-#   up           start db + app (+ the HTTPS proxy unless --private); the app runs the schema migrations on start
-#   data         copy the local database into the instance's (pg_dump → pg_restore, data only; refuses a non-empty
-#                target, `data --replace` wipes it first)
-#   deploy       build + push + up
-#   url          address and login (kept in deploy/aws/.env.vm)
-#   status | logs | ssh
-#   tunnel       SSH tunnel: app on http://127.0.0.1:8601, the instance's Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5434
-#   budget <email>   a $5 monthly cost alarm by e-mail (AWS Budgets; also one of the Free plan's credit activities)
-#   allow-my-ip  re-open SSH for your current IP (after it changed)
-#   stop | start     stop / start the instance (disk and data stay; the public IP changes → run `push` again for HTTPS)
-#   destroy      terminate the instance (its disk and all data on it), delete the security group and key pair
-# Settings (environment): AWS_REGION (eu-central-1), AWS_PROFILE (as the AWS CLI), INSTANCE_TYPE (t4g.small),
-# NAME (sharksight). DEPLOY_TARGET=local runs the remote steps in DEPLOY_LOCAL_DIR on this machine (to test the flow).
-set -euo pipefail
-ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
-HERE="$ROOT/deploy/aws"
-STACK="$ROOT/deploy"
-REGION="${AWS_REGION:-eu-central-1}"
-TYPE="${INSTANCE_TYPE:-t4g.small}"
-NAME="${NAME:-sharksight}"
-IMAGE="sharksight:prod-arm64"
-KEY="$HERE/$NAME.pem"                         # git-ignored (*.pem)
-ENV_VM="$HERE/.env.vm"                        # secrets for the instance; git-ignored (.env.*), 0600
-SSH_USER="ubuntu"
-TARGET="${DEPLOY_TARGET:-aws}"
-LOCAL_DIR="${DEPLOY_LOCAL_DIR:-/tmp/sharksight-vm}"
-REMOTE_DIR="sharksight"
-# compose project: its own name in local test mode, so it never touches the regular local stack ("sharksight")
-PROJECT_NAME="$( [[ "$TARGET" == local ]] && echo sharksight-vmtest || echo sharksight)"
-PRIVATE=0
-REPLACE=0
-die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
-need() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "$1 not found — $2"; }
-ec2()  { aws --region "$REGION" ec2 "$@"; }
-instance_id() {
-  ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=$NAME" \
-    "Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running,stopping,stopped" \
-    --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].InstanceId' --output text 2>/dev/null | grep -v None || true
-public_ip() {
-  if [[ "$TARGET" == "local" ]]; then echo "127.0.0.1"; return; fi
-  local id; id="$(instance_id)"; [[ -n "$id" ]] || die "no instance named $NAME in $REGION — run: deploy/aws/deploy.sh create"
-  ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$id" --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].PublicIpAddress' --output text
-ssh_opts() { echo "-i $KEY -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o UserKnownHostsFile=$HERE/.known_hosts -o ServerAliveInterval=30"; }
-# Run a shell command in the deployment directory on the instance (or locally with DEPLOY_TARGET=local).
-remote() {
-  if [[ "$TARGET" == "local" ]]; then
-    # local test mode: other host ports, so it runs beside the regular local stack and other local Postgres servers
-    mkdir -p "$LOCAL_DIR" && (cd "$LOCAL_DIR" && COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME="$PROJECT_NAME" DB_HOST_PORT=5435 APP_HOST_PORT=8602 \
-      HTTP_PORT=8088 HTTPS_PORT=8448 DOCKER="docker" bash -c "$1")
-  else
-    # shellcheck disable=SC2046
-    ssh $(ssh_opts) "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)" \
-      "mkdir -p ~/$REMOTE_DIR && cd ~/$REMOTE_DIR && COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=$PROJECT_NAME DOCKER='sudo docker' bash -c $(printf '%q' "$1")"
-  fi
-# Copy local files into the deployment directory (keeps the last path component).
-remote_copy() {
-  if [[ "$TARGET" == "local" ]]; then
-    mkdir -p "$LOCAL_DIR" && cp -R "$@" "$LOCAL_DIR/"
-  else
-    # shellcheck disable=SC2046
-    scp $(ssh_opts) -r -C "$@" "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip):$REMOTE_DIR/"
-  fi
-# Stream stdin into a command on the instance.
-remote_pipe() {
-  if [[ "$TARGET" == "local" ]]; then
-    bash -c "$1"
-  else
-    # shellcheck disable=SC2046
-    ssh $(ssh_opts) "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)" "$1"
-  fi
-env_get() { grep -E "^$1=" "$2" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true; }
-docker_cmd() { [[ "$TARGET" == local ]] && echo docker || echo 'sudo docker'; }
-cmd_check() {
-  need docker "install Docker Desktop or OrbStack"
-  [[ -f "$ROOT/.env" ]] || die "no .env at the repo root (see .env.example)"
-  if [[ "$TARGET" == "aws" ]]; then
-    need aws "brew install awscli, then: aws configure (or aws configure sso)"
-    local who; who="$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Arn --output text 2>/dev/null)" || die "not logged in: aws configure"
-    say "AWS identity $who, region $REGION, instance type $TYPE"
-  fi
-  say "ok"
-cmd_create() {
-  [[ "$TARGET" == "aws" ]] || die "create only makes sense on AWS"
-  [[ -z "$(instance_id)" ]] || die "an instance named $NAME already exists in $REGION"
-  if [[ ! -f "$KEY" ]]; then
-    say "key pair $NAME…"
-    ec2 delete-key-pair --key-name "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
-    ( umask 077; ec2 create-key-pair --key-name "$NAME" --key-type ed25519 --query KeyMaterial --output text > "$KEY" )
-  fi
-  local vpc sg ami myip userdata
-  vpc="$(ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=isDefault,Values=true --query 'Vpcs[0].VpcId' --output text)"
-  [[ "$vpc" != None ]] || die "no default VPC in $REGION"
-  sg="$(ec2 describe-security-groups --filters "Name=group-name,Values=$NAME" "Name=vpc-id,Values=$vpc" \
-        --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' --output text)"
-  if [[ "$sg" == None ]]; then
-    say "security group $NAME (SSH from your IP, 80/443 open)…"
-    sg="$(ec2 create-security-group --group-name "$NAME" --vpc-id "$vpc" \
-          --description "SharkSight: SSH from the owner's IP, HTTPS proxy on 80/443" --query GroupId --output text)"
-    ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id "$sg" --ip-permissions \
-      'IpProtocol=tcp,FromPort=80,ToPort=80,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=0.0.0.0/0}]' \
-      'IpProtocol=tcp,FromPort=443,ToPort=443,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=0.0.0.0/0}]' >/dev/null
-  fi
-  myip="$(curl -fsS https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '[:space:]')"
-  ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id "$sg" --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr "$myip/32" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
-  ami="$(aws --region "$REGION" ssm get-parameters \
-         --names /aws/service/canonical/ubuntu/server/24.04/stable/current/arm64/hvm/ebs-gp3/ami-id \
-         --query 'Parameters[0].Value' --output text)"
-  userdata="$(mktemp)"
-  cat > "$userdata" <<'EOS'
-#!/bin/bash
-set -e
-if ! command -v docker >/dev/null; then curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh; fi
-if [ ! -f /swapfile ]; then
-  fallocate -l 2G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap /swapfile && swapon /swapfile
-  echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' >> /etc/fstab
-fi
-EOS
-  say "instance $TYPE ($ami)…"
-  local id
-  id="$(ec2 run-instances --image-id "$ami" --instance-type "$TYPE" --key-name "$NAME" --security-group-ids "$sg" \
-        --block-device-mappings 'DeviceName=/dev/sda1,Ebs={VolumeSize=20,VolumeType=gp3,DeleteOnTermination=true}' \
-        --credit-specification CpuCredits=standard --metadata-options HttpTokens=required \
-        --user-data "file://$userdata" \
-        --tag-specifications "ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=$NAME},{Key=project,Value=sharksight}]" \
-                             "ResourceType=volume,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=$NAME},{Key=project,Value=sharksight}]" \
-        --query 'Instances[0].InstanceId' --output text)"
-  rm -f "$userdata"
-  ec2 wait instance-running --instance-ids "$id"
-  say "running: $id at $(public_ip). Docker installs on first boot (~2 min); then: deploy/aws/deploy.sh deploy"
-cmd_allow_my_ip() {
-  local sg myip
-  sg="$(ec2 describe-security-groups --filters "Name=group-name,Values=$NAME" --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' --output text)"
-  myip="$(curl -fsS https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '[:space:]')"
-  ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id "$sg" --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr "$myip/32" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
-  say "SSH open for $myip"
-cmd_build() {
-  say "building $IMAGE (linux/arm64)…"
-  docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 --target prod -t "$IMAGE" --load "$ROOT"
-write_env() {
-  # Secrets for the instance, from the local .env; the web login is generated once and kept in .env.vm.
-  local ip site user pw hash
-  ip="$(public_ip)"
-  site="$( [[ "$TARGET" == local ]] && echo ':80' || echo "${ip//./-}.sslip.io")"   # HTTPS via sslip.io (local: HTTP)
-  user="$(env_get BASIC_AUTH_USER "$ENV_VM")"; user="${user:-pm}"
-  pw="$(env_get WEB_PASSWORD "$ENV_VM")"
-  [[ -n "$pw" ]] || pw="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"   # no pipe: under pipefail a SIGPIPE'd generator would end the script
-  hash="$(docker run --rm caddy:2.10-alpine caddy hash-password --plaintext "$pw")"
-  ( umask 077
-    { echo "# generated by deploy/aws/deploy.sh — secrets for the instance, never commit"
-      for k in OPENAI_API_KEY OPENAI_MODEL_FAST OPENAI_MODEL_SMART OPENAI_MODEL_EMBED POSTGRES_PASSWORD APP_DB_PASSWORD; do
-        echo "$k=$(env_get "$k" "$ROOT/.env")"
-      done
-      echo "APP_IMAGE=$IMAGE"
-      echo "SITE_ADDRESS=$site"
-      echo "BASIC_AUTH_USER=$user"
-      echo "BASIC_AUTH_HASH='$hash'"   # single quotes: compose must not expand the $ in the bcrypt hash
-      echo "WEB_PASSWORD=$pw"          # for you; the proxy only knows the hash
-cmd_push() {
-  [[ -n "$(docker images -q "$IMAGE")" ]] || die "no $IMAGE image — run: deploy/aws/deploy.sh build"
-  write_env
-  remote 'true'   # make sure the deployment directory exists
-  say "sending the image…"
-  docker save "$IMAGE" | gzip -1 | remote_pipe "gunzip | $(docker_cmd) load"
-  local staged; staged="$(mktemp -d)"
-  cp "$STACK/compose.yaml" "$STACK/Caddyfile" "$staged/"
-  cp "$ENV_VM" "$staged/.env"
-  mkdir -p "$staged/data" "$staged/restore"
-  [[ -f "$ROOT/data/settings.json" ]] && cp "$ROOT/data/settings.json" "$staged/data/"
-  [[ -d "$ROOT/data/models" ]] && cp -R "$ROOT/data/models" "$staged/data/"
-  say "copying compose, Caddyfile, .env, settings and 3D models…"
-  remote_copy "$staged/compose.yaml" "$staged/Caddyfile" "$staged/.env" "$staged/data" "$staged/restore"
-  rm -rf "$staged"
-  remote 'chmod 600 .env'
-cmd_up() {
-  local profile=""; [[ $PRIVATE == 1 ]] || profile="--profile public"
-  remote "\$DOCKER compose $profile up -d && \$DOCKER compose ps --format '{{.Name}} {{.Status}}'"
-  if [[ $PRIVATE == 1 ]]; then say "private: reach it with deploy/aws/deploy.sh tunnel"; else cmd_url; fi
-cmd_data() {
-  say "dumping the local database…"
-  make -C "$ROOT" backup >/dev/null
-  local dump; dump="$(ls -t "$ROOT"/data/backups/sharksight-*.dump | head -1)"
-  remote "\$DOCKER compose up -d --wait db app >/dev/null"   # the app creates the schema (migrations) on start
-  local rows
-  rows="$(remote "\$DOCKER compose exec -T db psql -U sharksight -d sharksight -tAc 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_item'" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
-  if [[ "$rows" != "0" ]]; then
-    [[ $REPLACE == 1 ]] || die "the instance's database already holds $rows source items — use: deploy/aws/deploy.sh data --replace"
-    say "wiping the instance's database…"
-    remote "\$DOCKER compose down && \$DOCKER volume rm ${PROJECT_NAME}_pgdata && \$DOCKER compose up -d --wait db app >/dev/null"
-  fi
-  say "copying $(basename "$dump") ($(du -h "$dump" | cut -f1))…"
-  remote_copy "$dump"
-  remote "mv $(basename "$dump") restore/db.dump && \$DOCKER compose stop app >/dev/null && \
-    \$DOCKER compose exec -T db sh -c 'pg_restore -l /restore/db.dump | grep -v alembic_version > /tmp/list && \
-      pg_restore -U sharksight -d sharksight --data-only --disable-triggers --single-transaction -L /tmp/list /restore/db.dump' && \
-    rm -f restore/db.dump && \$DOCKER compose start app >/dev/null && \
-    \$DOCKER compose exec -T db psql -U sharksight -d sharksight -tAc \"SELECT 'source items: ' || COUNT(*) FROM source_item\""
-  say "data copied"
-cmd_url() {
-  local site user pw
-  site="$(env_get SITE_ADDRESS "$ENV_VM")"; user="$(env_get BASIC_AUTH_USER "$ENV_VM")"; pw="$(env_get WEB_PASSWORD "$ENV_VM")"
-  if [[ "$site" == :* ]]; then site="http://127.0.0.1:8088"; else site="https://$site"; fi
-  say "$site   login: $user / $pw   (the HTTPS certificate takes a minute on first start)"
-cmd_tunnel() {
-  say "app → http://127.0.0.1:8601   Postgres → 127.0.0.1:5434 (Ctrl-C to close)"
-  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
-cmd_budget() {
-  local email="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$email" ]] || die "usage: deploy/aws/deploy.sh budget <email>"
-  local account; account="$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)"
-  aws budgets create-budget --account-id "$account" \
-    --budget '{"BudgetName":"sharksight-5usd","BudgetLimit":{"Amount":"5","Unit":"USD"},"TimeUnit":"MONTHLY","BudgetType":"COST"}' \

-    --notifications-with-subscribers "[{\"Notification\":{\"NotificationType\":\"ACTUAL\",\"ComparisonOperator\":\"GREATER_THAN\",\"Threshold\":80,\"ThresholdType\":\"PERCENTAGE\"},\"Subscribers\":[{\"SubscriptionType\":\"EMAIL\",\"Address\":\"$email\"}]}]"
-  say "budget sharksight-5usd: e-mail to $email at 80 % of \$5 a month"
-cmd_destroy() {
-  read -r -p "Terminate $NAME in $REGION (its disk and ALL data on it), delete its security group and key pair? [y/N] " ok
-  local id; id="$(instance_id)"
-  if [[ -n "$id" ]]; then ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids "$id" >/dev/null; ec2 wait instance-terminated --instance-ids "$id"; fi
-  local sg; sg="$(ec2 describe-security-groups --filters "Name=group-name,Values=$NAME" --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' --output text)"
-  [[ "$sg" == None ]] || ec2 delete-security-group --group-id "$sg"
-  ec2 delete-key-pair --key-name "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
-  rm -f "$KEY" "$HERE/.known_hosts"
-  say "destroyed"
-cmd="${1:-help}"; shift || true
-args=()
-for a in "$@"; do
-  case "$a" in --private) PRIVATE=1 ;; --replace) REPLACE=1 ;; --*) die "unknown option $a" ;; *) args+=("$a") ;; esac
-done
-case "$cmd" in
-  check|create|build|push|up|data|url|tunnel|destroy) "cmd_$cmd" ;;
-  allow-my-ip) cmd_allow_my_ip ;;
-  budget) cmd_budget "${args[@]:-}" ;;
-  deploy) cmd_build; cmd_push; cmd_up ;;
-  status) remote '$DOCKER compose ps' ;;
-  logs)   remote '$DOCKER compose logs --tail 200' ;;
-  ssh)    # shellcheck disable=SC2046
-          ssh $(ssh_opts) "$SSH_USER@$(public_ip)" ;;
-  stop)   ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids "$(instance_id)" >/dev/null && say "stopping (disk and data stay)" ;;
-  start)  ec2 start-instances --instance-ids "$(instance_id)" >/dev/null && ec2 wait instance-running --instance-ids "$(instance_id)" \
-            && say "running at $(public_ip) — the IP changed: run push (new HTTPS address), then up" ;;
-esac
